questions.question: What is constitutional law?
options: Criminal law
The body of law that defines the relationship between different entities within a state
Civil law
International law
questions.explanation: Constitutional law defines the relationship between different entities within a state, including the executive, legislature, and judiciary.

questions.question: What is separation of powers?
options: The division of government responsibilities into distinct branches
The power of the president
The role of the judiciary
The function of the legislature
questions.explanation: Separation of powers is the division of government responsibilities into distinct branches to prevent any one branch from exercising the core functions of another.

questions.question: What is judicial review?
options: The power of courts to examine and invalidate unconstitutional actions
The power of the president to review laws
The power of Congress to review court decisions
The power of states to review federal laws
questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine and invalidate actions of the legislative and executive branches if they are unconstitutional.

questions.question: What is due process?
options: The right to a speedy trial
The legal requirement that the state must respect all legal rights owed to a person
The right to bear arms
The right to free speech
questions.explanation: Due process is the legal requirement that the state must respect all legal rights owed to a person, including fair treatment through the judicial system.

questions.question: What is the supremacy clause?
options: A clause that gives states power over the federal government
A clause that establishes federal law as the supreme law of the land
A clause that gives the president supreme power
A clause that gives Congress supreme power
questions.explanation: The supremacy clause establishes federal law as the supreme law of the land, overriding state laws.
